title: Republic of Cabo Verde
capsule: The Republic of Cabo Verde (República de Cabo Verde) is an archipelago state of ten volcanic islands in the central Atlantic, roughly 570 km west of Senegal, uninhabited before Portuguese settlement from 1462. The islands gained independence from Portugal on 5 July 1975 under the PAIGC/PAICV movement, initially in a one-party framework aligned with Guinea-Bissau; a constitutional revision in 1990–1991 introduced multiparty democracy and peaceful electoral alternation. Cabo Verde's strategic mid-Atlantic position made it a critical waystation in the Atlantic slave trade and later in twentieth-century transatlantic aviation. It is classified as a lower-middle-income country with one of Africa's more stable democratic records.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The modern state's extent (the ten islands) is unambiguous; historical political boundaries within colonial-era divisions are fully documented in Portuguese and post-independence sources.
